 Cabinet extends Fast Track Special Courts Scheme till 2031: Key facts, Background, Major Objectives and Challenges 
 Why in news? 
 On 4 November 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the continuation and expansion of the Fast Track Special Courts Scheme for the period 2026-27 to 2030–31. 
 Key Facts 
 Particular 
 Details 
 Scheme 
 Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) 
 Approved by 
 Union Cabinet 
 Approval date 
 4 November 2026 
 Extension period 
 1 April 2026-31 March 2031 
 Total duration 
 5 years 
 Existing courts 
 779 
 Proposed courts 
 850 
 Additional courts 
 71 
 Total financial outlay 
 ₹ 3,788.04 crore

 ₹ 2,353.15 crore 
 States/UTs share 
 ₹ 1,434.89 crore 
 Central funding source 
 Nirbhaya Fund

 Department of Justice 
 Main beneficiaries 
 Women and children who are victims of sexual offences 
 What are Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs)? 
 Dedicated courts established to ensure the speedy trial and disposal of specific categories of criminal cases. 
 In India, Fast Track Special Courts under this centrally sponsored scheme primarily deal with pending rape cases and cases involving sexual offences against children under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. 
 These courts aim to reduce delays in judicial proceedings by providing dedicated judicial officers, prosecutors and supporting personnel. 
 Major Objectives of FTSCs 
 Speedy Justice: Ensure faster disposal of rape and POCSO cases. 
 Reduce Pendency: Reduce the backlog of pending sexual offence cases. 
 Victim Protection : Provide a safe and supportive environment for survivors. 
 Child-Friendly Justice: Facilitate sensitive handling of child victims. 
 Judicial Efficiency: Improve the efficiency of the criminal justice system through dedicated resources. 
 Background: When and Why Was the Scheme Launched? 
 The Fast Track Special Courts Scheme was launched on 2 October 2019 by the Central Government. 
 Its introduction was closely associated with the need to strengthen the judicial mechanism for dealing with sexual offences, particularly following the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018. 
 Important developments 
 2012: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act was enacted. 
 2013 : Criminal Law (Amendment) Act strengthened legal provisions relating to sexual offences. 
 2018: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act introduced stricter provisions, including enhanced punishment for rape and sexual offences against children. 
 25 July 2019 : Supreme Court issued directions in Suo Motu Writ (Criminal) No. 1/2019 regarding special courts for POCSO cases. 
 2 October 2019: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Fast Track Special Courts was launched. 
 2026: Union Cabinet approved its continuation until 31 March 2031 and expansion to 850 courts. 
 Supreme Court's Role 
 On 25 July 2019, the Supreme Court issued directions in Suo Motu Writ (Criminal) No. 1/2019 concerning the establishment of exclusive Special Courts in districts having more than 100 pending cases under the POCSO Act. 
 This direction became an important foundation for the establishment of dedicated Fast Track Special Courts across the country.  
 Financial Structure of the Scheme 
 The government has approved a total financial outlay of ₹ 3,788.04 crore for the five-year extension. 
 The funding will be shared between the Central Government and participating States/UTs. 
 What is the Nirbhaya Fund? 
 The Nirbhaya Fund is a non-lapsable corpus established by the Government of India in 2013 to support initiatives aimed at improving the safety and security of women. 
 It was created following the 2012 Delhi gang rape case, which generated nationwide concern about women's safety.

 What is the POCSO Act, 2012? 
 The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 is a special legislation enacted to protect children from sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography. 
 It came into force on 14 November 2012. 
 The Act provides a child-friendly system for reporting, recording evidence, investigation and trial of offences.

 What are Vulnerable Witness Deposition Centres (VWDCs)? 
 These centres aim to provide a supportive environment for vulnerable witnesses, particularly children and survivors of sexual offences, while recording their statements. 
 Key Features are:   
 Safe Environment: Provides a more comfortable environment for vulnerable witnesses. 
 Reduced Trauma: Helps reduce the psychological stress associated with court proceedings. 
 Privacy: Supports privacy and protection during testimony. 
 Child-Friendly Facilities: Encourages age-appropriate arrangements for child witnesses. 
 Better Testimony Process : Helps witnesses participate in judicial proceedings with greater confidence. 
 Role of the Department of Justice in Implementation 
 Monitoring: Tracking the performance of FTSCs through the online FTSC Dashboard. 
 Progress Reviews: Collecting periodic reports from participating States and UTs. 
 Coordination: Consulting High Courts and State Governments. 
 Financial Monitoring: Reviewing expenditure statements and utilisation of funds. 
 Expansion: Identifying additional districts based on case pendency. 
 Performance Evaluation: Monitoring disposal of pending rape and POCSO cases. 
 Challenges in the Effective Implementation of FTSCs 
 Judicial Vacancies: Shortage of judges can affect the functioning of specialised courts. 
 Infrastructure Gaps: Several districts require better courtrooms and supporting facilities. 
 Increasing Case Pendency: New cases may continue to enter the judicial system faster than cases are disposed of. 
 Victim Protection: Survivors may face social stigma, intimidation and psychological pressure during trials. 
 Quality of Investigation: Delays in investigation and collection of evidence can slow down trials even in specialised courts. 
 Prelims MCQ 
 Q. With reference to Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), consider the following statements: 
 The scheme was launched in October 2019. 
 The scheme deals with pending rape and POCSO Act cases. 
 The Central Government's contribution under the extended scheme will be funded through the Nirbhaya Fund. 
 Which of the statements given above are correct? 
 A. 1 and 2 only
B. 2 and 3 only
C. 1 and 3 only
D. 1, 2 and 3 
 Mains Practice Question 
 Q. Critically examine the role of the POCSO Act, 2012, in protecting children from sexual offences.  
 FAQs 
 What is the Fast Track Special Courts Scheme? 
 Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2019 to ensure speedy trials of pending rape and POCSO Act cases. 
 When was the scheme extended until 2031? 
 On 4 November 2026. 
 How many Fast Track Special Courts are proposed under the extended scheme? 
 A total of 850 courts, compared with the existing 779. 
 Which fund will finance the Central Government's contribution? 
 The Nirbhaya Fund. 
 When was the POCSO Act implemented? 
 14 November 2012. 
 Indian Universities Slip in QS Asia Rankings; No IIT or IISc in Top 50 
 Why in News? 
 Indian universities have failed to secure a place in the top 50 of the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027 for the second consecutive year. The rankings, released by QS Quacquarelli Symonds, show that all six of India's highest-ranked institutions have slipped in the latest edition. 
 Despite the decline in rankings, India has increased its overall representation, with 325 universities featured in the list, compared to 294 in the previous year. 
 Key Highlights of QS Asia University Rankings 2027 
 No Indian university in the Top 50: For the second consecutive year, no Indian institution has secured a position among Asia's top 50 universities. 
 IIT Delhi leads India: IIT Delhi is India's highest-ranked institution at 66th position, down from 59th last year. 
 IISc Bengaluru: Its ranking has dropped from 64th to 79th. 
 IIT Bombay: It has slipped from 71st to 83rd position. 
 IIT Madras: Its position has declined from 70th to 85th. 
 IIT Kharagpur: It has fallen from 77th to 90th. 
 IIT Kanpur: It has dropped from 77th to 99th. 
 Delhi University: It has moved from 95th to 106th position, falling outside the top 100. 
 India's Growing Presence in Asian Rankings 
 Despite the decline in the positions of leading institutions, India's overall representation in the QS Asia Rankings has increased significantly. 
 India has 325 universities in the 2027 rankings, compared to 294 in 2026. 
 India is the second most represented higher education system in Asia. 
 The latest edition includes 34 new Indian universities. 
 Since 2016, the number of ranked Indian institutions has increased from 24 to 325, representing growth of more than 1,250%. 
 This growth is higher than that of several other major Asian higher education systems, including China, Indonesia, Japan and South Korea. 
 India's Strengths in Research and Doctoral Education 
 Although Indian universities have slipped in overall rankings, the country continues to perform strongly in research output and doctoral education. 
 1. Strong Research Output 
 India leads Asia in research output relative to academic staff, measured through the QS Papers per Faculty indicator. 
 A total of 27 Indian universities feature in Asia's top 50 for this indicator. 
 Five Indian universities are among the top 10, while two are in the top five. 
 2. Strength in Doctoral Education 
 Fifteen Indian universities share the first position in Asia for the proportion of academic staff holding PhD qualifications. 
 This highlights India's growing capacity in advanced research and higher education. 
 Research Impact Remains a Major Challenge 
 Despite strong research output, India has not achieved comparable performance in research impact. 
 Only three Indian universities feature in Asia's top 50 for Citations per Paper. 
 This indicator measures how frequently published research is cited by other researchers. 
 The gap suggests that higher research output has not yet translated into equally strong global research recognition and influence. 
 Indian Universities That Improved Their Rankings 
 While most leading Indian institutions experienced a decline, some universities improved their positions. 
 These include: 
 Chandigarh University 
 Lovely Professional University 
 Jamia Millia Islamia 
 What Did QS Say? 
 QS Senior Vice-President Ben Sowter highlighted India's growing research capacity but emphasised the need to improve research impact and international recognition. 
 According to him, India has established a strong foundation in research, but it must now focus on translating research output into greater academic influence and international recognition. 
 Conclusion 
 The QS Asia University Rankings 2027 present a mixed picture of India's higher education system. The increasing number of Indian universities in the rankings reflects the expansion of higher education and research capacity. However, the decline of leading institutions highlights the need to improve research quality, citations, international collaboration and global academic reputation. 
 India must focus not only on increasing the number of ranked universities but also on improving their overall academic performance and international competitiveness. 
 Prelims Practice Question  
 1. With reference to the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027, consider the following statements: 
 QS Quacquarelli Symonds releases the QS World University Rankings. 
 IIT Delhi is the highest-ranked Indian institution in the QS Asia Rankings 2027. 
 India has the highest number of universities in Asia's top 50 for Citations per Paper. 
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct? 
 (a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3 
 Mains Practice Question 
 Q. Despite significant growth in research output and doctoral capacity, Indian universities continue to face challenges in global academic rankings. Discuss the major reasons behind this gap and suggest measures to improve the global competitiveness of India's higher education system. 
 FAQs 
 1. What is the QS World University Rankings: Asia? 
 It is an annual ranking of Asian universities released by QS Quacquarelli Symonds to evaluate their academic performance, research, internationalisation and other indicators. 
 2. Which is India's highest-ranked institution in the QS Asia Rankings 2027? 
 IIT Delhi is India's highest-ranked institution, securing the 66th position. 
 3. How many Indian universities are included in the QS Asia Rankings 2027? 
 A total of 325 Indian universities feature in the rankings, compared to 294 in the previous year. 
 4. What is the Papers per Faculty indicator? 
 It measures research output relative to the number of academic staff at a university. 
 5. What does Citations per Paper measure? 
 It measures the research impact of published academic papers based on how frequently other researchers cite them.
